title: Autotune: workload-aware batching profile recommender and safe apply/rollback
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Problem: Serving costs for text-generation endpoints vary widely with request size distribution and model latency characteristics. Manual batching/caching tuning is slow, error-prone, and hard to keep optimal as traffic shifts. Goal: build an automated recommender that profiles real traffic to propose and safely roll out continuous-batching and KV-cache knob changes that reduce per-token cost without violating latency SLOs or harming quality.

Scope: prototype an engine that (1) collects lightweight workload signals (requests/sec, input token histogram, sequence length percentiles, cold vs warm cache share, model variant), (2) computes recommended continuous-batching parameters (target_batch_size distribution, max_delay_ms, token-aware batching thresholds, weight for prefix caching), (3) produces a ranked set of candidate configs with estimated cost/latency trade-offs, and (4) provides a safe apply workflow with canary rollout, automated health checks, and automatic rollback triggers.

Non-goals: this ticket does not include UI for complex multi-tenant allocation; initial rollout aims at internal prod stage and a small set of customer-facing routes for evaluation. Integration with cost-charging and billing will be handled in a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Agent can compute per-route workload profiles from 7-day sliding window and store summarized histogram blobs (percentiles for input tokens, requests/sec distribution)
Recommender returns a ranked list of >=3 batching+cache configs per route with estimated median latency and 95th percentile latency delta and estimated cost delta
Automatic candidate scoring uses heuristics: p50 latency target, p95 tail guardrails, and cost-per-token improvement >= 5% for first candidate
Safe apply executes a canary on 1% traffic for 30 minutes with health checks (error rate, p95 latency, quality regression probe) and auto-rollbacks if thresholds breached
Config snapshotting and rollback API available; rollback restores previous kernel and quantization-compatible profile and resumes traffic in <2 minutes
Integration tests cover simulated traffic profiles (burst, long-tail, cache-warmup) and verify no regression in p95 beyond configured SLOs
notes_and_tradeoffs: Heuristics vs ML: start with deterministic heuristics (latency percentiles + token-count bucketing) to keep recommendations explainable and auditable. Leave ML models for future when we have labeled cost/quality outcomes.

KV cache interplay: aggressive batching increases chance of cache misses for prefix-cached sessions; we will model warm fraction and penalize configs that increase cold-cache compute cost beyond threshold
Visibility: show estimated risk (probability of SLO breach) alongside cost savings so PMs can choose risk bands
Rollback window: 30 minutes may be too short for some quality regressions — include optional extended monitoring hooks that run evaluation prompts against production variants for 24 hours post-apply
implementation_plan: 1) Telemetry: add per-route sampler that emits token-length histograms, cache-hit fraction, and request interarrival distribution to metrics pipeline (Prometheus + clickhouse summary)
2) Profiler: offline job that compacts raw telemetry into 7-day sliding profiles and produces summary blobs for recommender input

3) Recommender: deterministic engine that computes candidate configs using token-aware binning, target latency budget, and max_batch_size heuristic; produce scoring report with estimated latency/cost deltas
4) Safety layer: implement canary orchestration (1% traffic), health-check suite (error rate, p95, quality probes) and automated rollback policies; wire to console alerts
5) Testing & rollout: end-to-end tests with synthetic traffic, small internal rollout, iterate on heuristics and thresholds before customer-facing rollout
risks: Quality regressions: batching can change tokenization boundaries and prompt framing for stateful chat sessions — mitigate with targeted quality probes
Measurement noise: low-traffic routes may produce unstable recommendations — add minimum traffic thresholds and fallback to conservative defaults
Operational complexity: partial applies across model variants require careful config compatibility matrix to avoid serving invalid kernel paths
